doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Photo session: wagons, parades and goodbyes
title: Jackson Hall and the advertising wagon band
summary: They read a sign for Jackson Hall at Congress and Burgundy and identify Johnny Pijol among ten men on an advertising wagon.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Let's see what the wagon looks like. It's one of the old furniture. Can you read that sign, anyone, there? No, let me hold it up. I have a new one. Two heart dancing. Jackson Hall. Ray here.
Ray in that band.
Yeah.
Jackson Hall.
Jackson Hall. Jackson Hall.
Yeah, that's the Mike Shack place. Down here.
Jackson Hall.
Congress and Burgundy.
Congress and Burgundy. That was the hall. I don't remember.
Yeah. Congress and Burgundy. Jackson Hall. Oh, yeah. They were going to play a dance there that night.
They used to have. Yeah. They had a dancing school there. Three times a week. They had a dancing school. Yeah.
Six, seven. There's ten fellows all together here, I believe. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Counting the driver. Yeah. And two horses.
I used to do advertising for them, too, you know, and wagons and everything else, you know.
That's Johnny Pijol here.
Yeah.
He used to play pickled clarinet with you.
Standing there for the case. Right here.
Johnny played clarinet. That's Pijol. I don't remember none of them. I'll tell you the truth.
I don't, really.
It's a shame. They should have had. They should have been dated. That would have been the best. That's the same one for me. That would have been your best bet.
